headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can egress broadly while Botpress can install packages, creating default-path data, prompt, and workflow coupling without documented isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no browser and no shared channel is documented, while Botpress has no filesystem or message-queue surface shown. A prompt-injection path is therefore not evidenced as default. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of Airflow-produced text into Botpress, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Airflow output into Botpress prompts or knowledge sources
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or queue is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted Airflow output into Botpress
Add a provenance label to any transferred text
requires-engineering: add a trusted-content gate before Botpress ingests external text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, so any sensitive content it touches can leave the environment. Botpress shows no egress, but it can install packages and may still process imported content locally. Because no shared workspace is documented, leakage is not proven, but uncertainty about Airflow's outbound paths warrants medium severity.
conditions: IF Airflow is configured to process sensitive files or secrets
IF Airflow tasks send those contents to external services over broad egress
mitigations: Restrict Airflow egress with an allowlist
Avoid placing secrets in Airflow task inputs
Run Botpress without external connectors
Review outbound destinations in Airflow logs
requires-engineering: isolate both agents behind separate network policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow can make outbound API calls, while Botpress can install packages, but neither profile shows shared writable storage, git state, or overlapping mutable resources. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main risk is only if an operator later connects them to the same directory or deployment target.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Botpress package installation mutates a shared runtime used by Airflow
mitigations: Use separate deployment directories
Pin Botpress dependencies
Avoid shared git worktrees
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate automated outputs and Botpress is a chatbot platform that may consume those outputs as content. No verification or orchestration guard is documented, so if Botpress treats Airflow-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing responses or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress ingests Airflow-generated text without validation
IF downstream Botpress flows act on that text as facts or instructions
mitigations: Require human review before Botpress uses Airflow output
Add schema validation to transferred data
Mark Airflow output as untrusted by default
Log source provenance in Botpress
requires-engineering: insert a verification step between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and touch no declared regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced. Compliance risk is limited to future configuration changes, especially if Airflow starts handling regulated data and Botpress is connected to a different hosting region or retention policy.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent
IF the two agents are deployed under different residency or retention regimes
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings for each system
Verify deployment region before connecting them
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both stacks
